# Expected: #4766 "How can I build `dxil` and `dxcompiler` as a static library?"

## What is being asked

This is a build-system/API question, not a shader-compile bug report. There is no shader, no
`dxc` command line, and no compiler symptom to reproduce. The reporter asks whether `dxil` and
`dxcompiler` can be built and linked as static libraries instead of shared (`.dll`/`.so`), so a
consuming engine can statically link the whole dependency.

The first comment (MarijnS95, a contributor) narrows this to a concrete, checkable claim: that
dropping `SHARED` from `add_clang_library(dxcompiler SHARED ...)`
(`tools/clang/tools/dxcompiler/CMakeLists.txt`) is "pretty trivial", and asks whether the
project would accept committing a `STATIC` option. Two follow-on problems are raised: (1) CMake
consumers of a static target need the transitive static dependency list, and no self-contained
archive is produced; (2) `DllMain` must still run to trigger ELF constructor behaviour on Linux
even when statically linked.

## Repro quality

`prose-only` — no shader, no `cmd.txt`, and no `dxc` invocation is applicable. This is a
build-configuration/CMake question.

## What "still open" vs "resolved" means here

- **Resolved / no longer applicable** would mean: the repo now offers a supported, in-tree way
  to produce a static `dxcompiler`/`dxil` (an `option()`, a `STATIC` target, or documented
  build flags), so a reader would no longer need to hand-patch `CMakeLists.txt` or maintain an
  out-of-tree fork to do this. A maintainer statement declining to support it (with a reason)
  would also count as "resolved" in the sense of "answered", even though the capability itself
  remains unavailable.
- **Still open** means: `add_clang_library(dxcompiler SHARED ...)` and the `dxildll` target are
  still hardcoded to `SHARED` with no `option()` toggle, no maintainer has given an official
  position in the thread, and no linked PR added this capability.

## Not compiler-verifiable, but source/build-config verifiable

No `dxc` invocation can test "can this be built as a static library" — there is nothing to
compile. Per the skill's guidance for build-system issues, the producing instrument here is the
CMake source itself (which target type it hardcodes) and its git history (whether that has ever
changed, and whether any PR proposed changing it), not a shader compile. `match.json`/`cmd.txt`
are deliberately absent. Evidence is captured in `manual-case-cmake-history.txt`, generated by
`capture-cmake-history.py` so the exact commands are reproducible.

I will also check the issue's own cross-reference timeline for any linked PR or later issue that
resolves this, since a build-system feature request is exactly the kind of thing that could be
closed by an unlinked follow-up.
